speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, nausea, or changes in your urine appearance, such as it appearing bright red or cola-colored?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information; since you have a history of recurrent urinary tract infections, have you noticed any passage of small, pebble-like stones when you urinate, or do you experience sharp, colicky pain that radiates to your groin?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy.
REQUEST IMAGES: Renal_ultrasound_right.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows reddish appearance, 10-20 WBCs/HPF, too numerous to count RBCs, negative nitrites, and positive leukocyte esterase. Renal ultrasound right: Normal renal parenchyma, no evidence of stones or hydronephrosis.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
While the history of recurrent UTIs and right flank pain could suggest a stone or standard infection, your doctor's suggestion of Tuberculosis is concerning; do you have any systemic symptoms like night sweats, weight loss, or a chronic cough? Additionally, have you ever traveled to or lived in an area where TB is endemic?

REQUEST TEST: Urine_Culture_and_Sensitivity (looking for Acid-Fast Bacilli).
REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urine Culture and Sensitivity: Acid-Fast Bacilli detected. Chest X-Ray: No active pulmonary tuberculosis identified; no cavitation or infiltrates noted.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Renal Tuberculosis.

The detection of Acid-Fast Bacilli in your urine confirms an active Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection localized to the urinary tract, even without active pulmonary symptoms. This condition typically arises from the hematogenous spread of pulmonary TB to the kidneys, often presenting with sterile pyuria (though cultures are positive here) and flank pain. Do you have any known exposure to tuberculosis or a history of latent TB disease?
